mcqs.question: Which statement correctly compares double circulation in humans with the single circulation found in most fish?

options.A: In double circulation, blood passes through the heart twice per complete circuit, whereas in single circulation it passes through the heart only once.
options.B: In double circulation, oxygenated and deoxygenated blood mix in the same ventricle, while in single circulation they remain completely separate.
options.C: Double circulation has only one circuit, while single circulation has two distinct circuits.
options.D: In double circulation, blood is pumped solely to the lungs; in single circulation it is pumped solely to the body.

mcqs.answer: In double circulation, blood passes through the heart twice per complete circuit, whereas in single circulation it passes through the heart only once.
mcqs.explanation: Double circulation consists of two separate circuits – pulmonary and systemic – so the blood travels through the heart twice (right side then left side) before completing a full body circuit. In single circulation, as in most fish, blood passes through the heart only once before reaching the gills and then the body. The other options misstate the mixing of blood, the number of circuits, or the direction of flow.

mcqs.question: In the pulmonary circuit of humans, blood follows which correct sequence?

options.A: Right atrium → Right ventricle → Pulmonary artery → Lungs → Pulmonary veins → Left atrium
options.B: Right atrium → Right ventricle → Aorta → Lungs → Pulmonary veins → Left atrium
options.C: Left atrium → Left ventricle → Pulmonary artery → Lungs → Pulmonary veins → Right atrium
options.D: Right atrium → Pulmonary veins → Lungs → Pulmonary artery → Right ventricle → Left atrium

mcqs.answer: Right atrium → Right ventricle → Pulmonary artery → Lungs → Pulmonary veins → Left atrium
mcqs.explanation: Pulmonary circulation starts with deoxygenated blood entering the right atrium, moving to the right ventricle, then being pumped through the pulmonary artery to the lungs where gas exchange occurs. Oxygen‑rich blood returns via the pulmonary veins to the left atrium. Options B, C, and D place vessels or chambers in the wrong order, breaking the physiological pathway.

mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly describes the systemic circuit starting from the left atrium?

options.A: Left atrium → Left ventricle → Aorta → Body tissues → Superior/Inferior vena cava → Right atrium
options.B: Left atrium → Right ventricle → Pulmonary artery → Lungs → Pulmonary veins → Right atrium
options.C: Right atrium → Right ventricle → Aorta → Body tissues → Vena cava → Left atrium
options.D: Left atrium → Aorta → Left ventricle → Body tissues → Vena cava → Right atrium

mcqs.answer: Left atrium → Left ventricle → Aorta → Body tissues → Superior/Inferior vena cava → Right atrium
mcqs.explanation: In systemic circulation, oxygenated blood leaves the left atrium, passes to the left ventricle, is pumped into the aorta, travels through arteries to body tissues, returns via veins to the superior and inferior vena cava, and finally reaches the right atrium. Options B and C mix pulmonary and systemic pathways, while D places the aorta before the left ventricle, which is anatomically incorrect.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand separation of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood
mcqs.question: In the normal human heart, which chambers contain oxygenated blood and which contain deoxygenated blood?

options.A: Left atrium and left ventricle – oxygenated; right atrium and right ventricle – deoxygenated
options.B: Right atrium and right ventricle – oxygenated; left atrium and left ventricle – deoxygenated
options.C: All four chambers contain a mixture of both oxygenated and deoxygenated blood
options.D: Only the atria contain oxygenated blood, while the ventricles contain deoxygenated blood

mcqs.answer: Left atrium and left ventricle – oxygenated; right atrium and right ventricle – deoxygenated
mcqs.explanation: The right side of the heart (right atrium and right ventrature) receives deoxygenated blood from the body and pumps it to the lungs. The left side (left atrium and left ventricle) receives oxygen‑rich blood from the lungs and pumps it to the systemic circulation. Options B, C, and D contradict this fundamental anatomical separation.

mcqs.question: What is double circulation and how does it differ from the single circulation found in most fish?

options.A: Double circulation is the presence of two separate circuits—pulmonary and systemic—so that blood passes through the heart twice per complete circuit; unlike single circulation where blood passes through the heart only once.
options.B: Double circulation means the heart has two chambers; single circulation has one chamber.
options.C: In double circulation, oxygenated and deoxygenated blood mix completely; in single circulation they remain separate.
options.D: Double circulation occurs only in mammals, while single circulation occurs only in reptiles.

mcqs.answer: Double circulation is the presence of two separate circuits—pulmonary and systemic—so that blood passes through the heart twice per complete circuit; unlike single circulation where blood passes through the heart only once.
mcqs.explanation: Double circulation refers to the two distinct pathways: pulmonary (heart → lungs → heart) and systemic (heart → body → heart). This arrangement ensures that oxygenated and deoxygenated blood are kept separate and that the blood passes through the heart twice for each full body circuit. The other options misinterpret the structural or taxonomic aspects of circulation.

mcqs.question: When a person inhales oxygen‑rich air, which sequence correctly shows the path that this oxygen takes through the pulmonary circuit to reach the left side of the heart?

options.A: Right atrium → Right ventricle → Pulmonary artery → Lungs → Pulmonary veins → Left atrium
options.B: Right atrium → Pulmonary veins → Lungs → Pulmonary artery → Left atrium
options.C: Left atrium → Left ventricle → Aorta → Lungs → Pulmonary veins → Right atrium
options.D: Right ventricle → Pulmonary artery → Lungs → Pulmonary veins → Right atrium → Left atrium

mcqs.answer: Right atrium → Right ventricle → Pulmonary artery → Lungs → Pulmonary veins → Left atrium
mcqs.explanation: Oxygen‑poor blood enters the right atrium, moves to the right ventricle, and is pumped via the pulmonary artery to the lungs where it picks up oxygen. The oxygen‑rich blood then returns through the pulmonary veins to the left atrium. Options B, C, and D place vessels or chambers in an illogical order, breaking the physiological flow.

mcqs.question: During a marathon, oxygenated blood is delivered from the heart to the leg muscles. Which sequence correctly represents this systemic pathway?

options.A: Left atrium → Left ventricle → Aorta → Common iliac artery → Femoral artery → Muscle capillaries → Veins → Inferior vena cava → Right atrium
options.B: Right atrium → Right ventricle → Pulmonary artery → Lungs → Pulmonary veins → Left atrium
options.C: Left ventricle → Aorta → Coronary arteries → Heart muscle → Veins → Right atrium
options.D: Left atrium → Aorta → Carotid artery → Brain → Veins → Right atrium

mcqs.answer: Left atrium → Left ventricle → Aorta → Common iliac artery → Femoral artery → Muscle capillaries → Veins → Inferior vena cava → Right atrium
mcqs.explanation: Oxygen‑rich blood leaves the left atrium, passes to the left ventricle, is pumped into the aorta, then travels through the common iliac and femoral arteries to reach the leg muscles. After gas exchange, blood returns via veins to the inferior vena cava and finally to the right atrium. Options B describes the pulmonary circuit, C is the coronary circulation, and D involves the cerebral circulation, none of which describe delivery to leg muscles.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand separation of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood
mcqs.question: A diver surfaces rapidly and needs efficient delivery of oxygenated blood to his muscles. Which statement correctly describes the normal separation of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood in the heart that ensures this efficiency?

options.A: Oxygenated blood is confined to the left atrium and left ventricle, while deoxygenated blood is confined to the right atrium and right ventricle.
options.B: Oxygenated blood is confined to the right atrium and right ventricle, while deoxygenated blood is confined to the left atrium and left ventricle.
options.C: Both oxygenated and deoxygenated blood are mixed in all four chambers before being pumped out.
options.D: The separation occurs only in the atria; the ventricles contain a mixture of both types of blood.

mcqs.answer: Oxygenated blood is confined to the left atrium and left ventricle, while deoxygenated blood is confined to the right atrium and right ventricle.
mcqs.explanation: In a healthy heart, the right side (right atrium and ventricle) handles deoxygenated blood returning from the body, sending it to the lungs. The left side (left atrium and ventricle) handles oxygenated blood returning from the lungs, sending it to systemic tissues. This strict separation prevents mixing and allows rapid, efficient oxygen delivery. Options B, C, and D describe abnormal or incorrect arrangements.
